raw_text: member_002 (独立复核) here. No candidate is published yet, so I'm on standby for independent review. Please publish your fixed candidate with fix_patch and send me handoff_patch with the patch_id when ready. I will integrate_patch, run the same-version public tests, and then org_review_patch (accept or request changes with concrete findings). Note: the issue concerns seaborn/_core/scales.py ScalarFormatter offset handling (log-scale legend/labels losing multiplicative offset, e.g. 1e6 ranges), plus likely _core/scales.py ContinuousBase._get_formatter/_setup; relevant rcParams are axes.formatter.useoffset and offset_threshold. Please include or point to tests covering both the objects interface legend and scatterplot legend.

Final candidate patch-1 published (source version v18, files_sha256 edf037666e84265e6c40359f4ec674c09087b953451d605c4b11e4179bd429ba). Please integrate_patch, run same-version public tests, then org_review_patch.

Changed paths (2): seaborn/_core/scales.py, tests/_core/test_scales_offset_probe.py.

Fix summary: Continuous._legend in seaborn/_core/scales.py formatted locs with axis.major.formatter.format_ticks(locs) and dropped the ScalarFormatter offset, so labels for ~1e6 ranges read as "1.0, 1.05, ...". New helper _format_legend_labels(formatter, locs) formats ticks first (offset is only populated as a side effect of formatting), reads get_offset() defensively via getattr, parses mathtext forms ("$1e6$", "\mathdefault{1e6}") via _parse_offset, and rescales each relative numeric label back to full magnitude via _apply_offset (%g). Non-numeric labels untouched; when the factor is ~1 output is identical to before, so no regression for ordinary ranges.

Coverage rationale: Plotter._update_legend_contents (seaborn/_core/plot.py:1562) reads scales[var]._legend, so both so.Plot and classic scatterplot share this single fix site — the issue's two reproduction paths.

My own evidence on exactly this content: run_tests selection {tests/_core/test_scales_offset_probe.py, tests/_core/test_scales.py, tests/_core/test_plot.py} -> validation_status verified, collected 264, 258 passed, 6 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 errors. The two new tests cover offset-applied (labels full magnitude, match locs) and no-offset cases with an rcParams-restoring fixture.

Please verify independently, especially: (1) actual label text for the 1e6 case, (2) that a scatterplot legend shows full magnitude, (3) no behavior change when useoffset is False. If you find anything wrong, request changes with concrete findings and I will rework.

Review recorded: review-1 = ACCEPT for patch-1 (files_sha256 edf037666e84265e6c40359f4ec674c09087b953451d605c4b11e4179bd429ba). Evidence: I integrated patch-1 into my private tree with no conflicts, then ran the public frontend on that exact version (report test-report-0dd540ab5538d2261a9f2458): 114 collected, 113 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed, validation_status=verified. Scope included tests/_core/test_scales_offset_probe.py (both new tests), tests/_core/test_scales.py and tests/test_relational.py legend/log/scatter selections.

Takeaway for delivery: acceptance does not merge into your tree, so you must still finish on YOUR final version: if your tree already equals patch-1 content, just run_tests (full or a clearly relevant selection) on that version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Current delivery_status for my copy shows fixed_patch_id null; only you (designated delivery member) can close the loop.

Non-blocking follow-up idea (optional, don't destabilize a green version for it): _apply_offset re-renders numeric labels with f"{value:g}" instead of re-formatting the actual value through the formatter, so label text style can differ from axis ticks in edge cases (very small/large magnitudes, thousands separators). If you have budget left a cleaner form might be to compute locs*factor and pass those through formatter.format_ticks with useOffset temporarily disabled, but the current behavior is correct for the reported ~1e6 case and I am not requesting changes.
